brief: Weekly overview note. Quarter-end flow rebalancing plus softer core PCE, a more nuanced Fed tone, and jobs data undercutting stagflation fears led Goldman to push out its October hike forecast, and US 10y/30y yields may have seen near-term exhaustion yesterday. But a more concerning risk emerged: a disorderly European rates move, with French elections next year and less clear political leadership leaving Europe more exposed to market forces than the US. This week's rates move hit Goldman's 2-std-deviation monthly threshold for equities, with spillover into credit (HY's worst one-day decline in 18 months, higher credit vol). Rising yields are forcing fiscal discipline on governments while tightening conditions do central banks' work for them. Hedge funds are already defensively positioned, with net exposure in the 5th-9th percentile by lookback (0%-2% for US equities only). Separately, the Middle East catalyst calendar (midterms, Israeli elections) could shift the conflict's trajectory, with oil flow reportedly back near pre-March levels. On AI, Meta (+30% in September), Micron, new highs in Nvidia and the Nasdaq, and AMZN's addition to Goldman's Conviction List point to the trade broadening from capex to facilitators, with narrow breadth expected to persist as a feature of the next leg higher.
